question: Who wrote the medieval-era epic poem ‘Padmavat’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Malik Muhammad Jayasi.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Malik Muhammad Jayasi wrote the medieval-era epic poem ‘**Padmavat**’.
 
• He is a poet of the Nirguna Premashrayi stream of the Bhakti era of Hindi literature. 
 
 
• He was a resident of Jais in **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• The word Jayasi is used in his name as his surname.
 
• There are mentions of 21 of his compositions in which **Padmavat, Akhradan, Aakhri Kalam, Kaharnama, Chitrekha**, etc. are prominent.
 
• But he got famous with his Padmavat Granth.
 
• Its language is Awadhi and its style of composition, the Doha Chaupai method has influenced poets of ancient times.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mulla Daud** was the first poet in the ideology of Sufism belonging to Dalmau (Raebareli).

 
 
• His famous poem **"Laur Chanda"( or Chandayan) **was composed in the Avadhi language.
 
 
 
• **Amīr Khusrau **was an Indian Sufi singer, musician, poet and scholar who lived under the Delhi Sultanate.
 
 
• He was a mystic and a spiritual disciple of **Nizamuddin Auliya of Delhi.**
 
 
 
• **Abu'l Fadl and Abu'l-Fadl 'Allami,** was the **grand vizier of the Mughal emperor Akbar**.
 
 
• He was the author of the **Akbarnama**.
